variants.headline: Looking back: party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by {leader}, leader of {party}.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The leader of {party}, {leader}, had blundered in an election debate.

Workers deserve political debate about the conditions of their lives, not merely a competition in speaking neatly. A leader's blunder can deserve attention without displacing wages, safety and services from the argument. Labour should keep the standard practical and refuse to make a performance the whole measure of representation.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We criticise {target} in this assessment. Political leadership includes judgment under scrutiny, and a debate blunder is an appropriate occasion to question whether the standard of public presentation has been adequate.
